images.title: Fifths of a garden bed
images.purpose: Show that 2 fifths and 1 fifth are counts of the same unit, so together they make 3 fifths.
images.composition: One wide rectangular garden bed in the centre with wide margins, and one sum line centred below it.
images.exact_structure: One wide flat rectangular garden bed cut by straight vertical lines into 5 equal upright strips. From the left: strips 1 and 2 filled teal #0072B2, strip 3 filled amber #E69F00, strips 4 and 5 plain. A thin reddish purple #CC79A7 brace below strips 1 to 3 groups the 3 planted strips. Centred below: one sum line. No flowers drawn. Exactly 1 bed, 5 equal strips, 2 teal, 1 amber, 2 plain.

images.takeaway: Same unit: add the counts and keep the unit.
images.description: A garden bed in 5 equal strips: 2 teal strips and 1 amber strip are grouped by a brace, showing 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5 with the unit still one fifth.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one strip and say its size, then count the planted strips.

image_decisions.why: Counting strips of one size on the bed shows why the unit stays fifths.
